THIS MFA FILED U/S. 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY  THE IMPUGNED JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 29.11.2016 PASSED BY  THE MACT-XIII, VIJAYAPURA IN MVC NO.1455/2013.
 -2-  MFA No. 200961 of 2017  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the MACT, Vijayapura, in MVC.No.1455/2013 dated 29.11.2016.
02.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
03. The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the impugned judgment and award is contrary to law and material evidence before the Court.
The Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head loss of consortium to appellant No.1/Kavita (2nd wife).

Further he has submitted that the Tribunal has not taken into consideration future prospects as per decision of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On all these grounds, sought for allow the appeal.

04. As against this, learned counsel for respondent/insurance company has submitted his argument that one Sangeeta also wife (1st wife) of Bhimashankar Rokade, who is petitioner in MVC No.568/2013 had preferred appeal before the Hon'ble Division Bench of this court in MFA No.202263/2017 (MV), the same is already dismissed on 20.10.2020.
Hence, the present appeal is not maintainable in law.
On these grounds, sought for dismissal of this appeal.

05. Having heard arguments on both sides and on perusal of records, the following points arise for consideration:
(i) Whether appellant Nos.1 and 2 are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
(ii) Whether this appeal (MFA No.200961/2017) is maintainable in law in view of the judgment passed in MFA No.202263/2017 dated 20.10.2020?

(iii) What order/award?
06.

My findings to the above points are as under:

07. A perusal of impugned judgment in MVC No.1455/2013 the Tribunal in para-37 has observed as under:
37) The petitioners are entitled for the compensation amount under the relevant heads as under:
To the 1st wife Smt.Sangeeta:
1. Loss of dependency : Rs.4,62,910/-
2. Loss of consortium of married life : Rs.50,000/-
3. Transportation of dead Body & funeral expenses: Rs.25,000/-

Total : Rs.5,37,910/-
 rounded of to : Rs.5,38,000/-

To the 2nd wife Smt.Kavita:
 1. Loss of dependency : Rs.4,62,909/-
 2. Loss of love & affection : Rs. 50,000/-

Total : Rs.5,12,909/-
 Rounded off to Rs.5,13,000/-
To the son of deceased Pramod aged 2 years 1. Loss of dependency : Rs.4,62,909/-
2. Loss of love & affection : Rs. 50,000/-
3. loss of care & guidance of minor child : Rs. 50,000/-
Total : Rs.5,62,909/-
Rounded off to Rs.5,63,000/-
08.

A perusal of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has taken notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,781/-, but it has not added future prospects towards income of the deceased as per Pranay Sethi's case (supra).
At the time of accident, the age of deceased was 52 years as per Ex.P8/service register.

Hence, 15% has to be added Kavita W/O Bhimashankar Rokade And Anr vs Ramachandra Kishanrao Patil And Ors on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30720539/

sentences.text:
towards income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.18,148/-
(Rs.15,781/- + Rs.2,367/-); since there are two dependents 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.12,099/- (Rs.18,148/- (-)
Rs.6,049/-).

With these components, the loss of dependency works out to Rs.12,099/- x 12 x 11 =
Rs.15,97,068/- is awarded towards loss of dependency.

09. The Tribunal has awarded compensation in a sum of Rs.13,88,728/- towards loss of dependency and distributed equally to 1st wife/Sangeeta, 2nd wife/Kavita and minor son/Pramod equally i.e. an amount of Rs.4,62,909/- each of the claimants.
10. Now this Court has enhanced compensation towards loss of dependency from Rs.13,88,728/- to Rs.15,97,068/-.

Then in this appeal appellant No.2/Pramod is only entitled for enhancement of compensation in a sum of Rs.2,08,340/- (Rs.15,97,068/- (-) Rs.13,88,728/-).
11.

Accordingly, appellant No.2/Pramod is entitled to enhancement of compensation in a sum of Rs.2,08,340/- with interest at 6% p.a. (excluding amount of Rs.5,63,000/- granted by the Tribunal already awarded to appellant No.2/Pramod).
12. With regard to apportionment of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,37,910/- to the 1st wife/Smt.Sangeeta.
Being dissatisfied with judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, Smt.Sangeeta had preferred appeal before the Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.202263/2017 (MV).
The learned counsel for respondent has produced the copy of this judgment dated 20.10.2020.
In view of this judgment, appeal filed by Smt.Sangeeta was dismissed by the Division Bench of this Court.
Therefore, Smt.Sangeeta is not entitled for any enhancement of compensation.
13. The Tribunal has awarded compensation to the 2nd wife/Kavita in a sum of Rs.5,13,000/-.
The Division Bench has observed in para-7 of its judgment that the law in this country cannot countenance plurality of spouses for the purpose of mulcting the insurer with higher compensation.
In view of this judgment, since the appeal filed by the 1st wife/Sangeeta is already dismissed by the Division Bench, the 2nd wife/Kavita is not entitled for any enhancement of compensation.

14. With regard to enhancement of compensation in respect of appellant No.2/Pramod is concerned,
it is the duty of the Court to safeguard the interest of minor, though the 2nd wife/Kavita who is appellant No.1 in this case is not entitled for any enhancement compensation, the minor son/Pramod- appellant No.2 is legally entitled for enhancement of compensation.

Accordingly,
point No.2 is answered Partly in Affirmative.

15. For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
